subject: Art & Design
title: Dark Mode: Color in Low Light
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Dark Mode: Color in Low Light.

hook.text: Dark mode isn't just 'invert colors.' A pure white text on pure black background causes halation.

buildup.text: Halation makes bright text bloom and blur on dark backgrounds, especially for astigmatic users.

discovery.text: Best practice: use off-white (#E0E0E0) on dark gray (#121212), not pure white on pure black.

twist.text: Colors that look great in light mode can feel neon-harsh in dark mode. You need separate palettes.

climax.text: Material Design recommends reducing saturation by 10-20% for dark mode surfaces.

punchline.text: Dark mode isn't a toggle. It's a redesign.

quiz.question: Why shouldn't you use pure white text on pure black in dark mode?
options: It causes halation — bright text blooms and blurs
Pure black screens use more energy
It's impossible to render on modern screens

details.summary: Dark mode reverses the traditional light-background paradigm, using dark backgrounds with light text. It reduces eye strain in low-light environments, saves battery on OLED screens, and requires its own color system — colors that work on white backgrounds often fail on dark ones.
details.whyItMatters: With dark mode now standard on major platforms, designers must create dual color systems. Colors that pop on white can vibrate painfully on black.
takeaways: Dark backgrounds with light text reduce low-light eye strain
Colors must be adjusted — not simply inverted — for dark mode
Dark mode requires desaturation and distinct contrast ratios

faq.question: Is dark mode actually better for your eyes?
faq.answer: In low-light environments, dark mode reduces the bright light hitting your eyes, easing strain. But in bright environments, light mode is often easier to read. Dark mode also helps people sensitive to bright light. There's no one-size-fits-all answer — offering both modes is the best approach.

faq.question: Why can't you just invert colors for dark mode?
faq.answer: Pure white text on pure black creates excessive contrast that causes halation (glowing text) for many users. Saturated colors vibrate against dark backgrounds.
